explanation: This head is NOT broad. It fires on the comma that CLOSES a mid-sentence insertion that was OPENED by a comma: an appositive, a non-restrictive relative clause, a participial or prepositional aside, or a reporting tag ('The bridge, which was built in 1932[,]', 'The plan, in my view[,]', 'designed, according to Owens[,]'). From the closing comma it attends with weight about 1.0 back to the opening comma; in standalone sentences such closers measure about 0.4-0.6 x max, and up to 1.0 x max in long documents. Predict inactive (below 0.25 x max) for: single sentences of 10 tokens or fewer with no comma or with only an intro comma ('However,', 'In 2019,', 'After lunch,', 'When it rained,'); comma-free single sentences of up to about 21 tokens; opening commas; and insertions closed by a semicolon, a period or 'and' instead of a comma. Outside the inactive class, and weak at about 0.2-0.35 x max (they can cross the line): items and 'and' in comma lists ('apples, pears and plums'); dash-closed asides ('— built in 1932 —'); a closing comma whose aside opened without a comma or with a dash. The closing comma is also weak (about 0.05-0.25 x max) when the text itself opens with a bare name or a possessive subject ('Lena,', 'John,', 'Her friend,'), but it is strong again when an earlier sentence comes first or the subject starts with 'The', 'This' or 'A'.
